column1: # The Chinese occurrences this repository still carries in Go source, as a permission per rule and path.
# The boundary this ratchet enforces is data versus prose, and the rules name the two sides:
#   han-comment       Han or full-width punctuation inside a comment. Prose, in a repository whose prose is
#                     English; no occurrence is allowed and no entry may be added.
#   han-test-prose    the same runes inside a string literal passed to a testing helper, i.e. the message a
#                     failing run prints. Prose too, and likewise no occurrence is allowed.
#   han-literal       the same runes in any other string literal. This is where the data lives: a test
#                     fixture is a program, a path or an expected rendering, and the language's own text
#                     belongs in it. Each count below is a permission for one file, and the list can only
#                     shrink: a count that reaches zero must be deleted, because an entry that guards
#                     nothing is the last place in the tree that still says what the ratchet was for.
# Two things are not permissions and are carved out by the ratchet itself rather than allowed here: the
# generated catalog (internal/i18n/msg_gen.go, whose text is the message table's own data) and the
# generated C header (compiler/internal/rtcat/msg_c.h, which is not Go source at all). The language columns
# of internal/i18n/source/*.tsv are the other half of the data boundary and are not Go source either.
# The generator's own detector: a character class over the Han blocks, written as escapes because the
# runes are a pattern rather than text. It is read as a literal once unquoted, so it is counted here.
